Generate and benchmark synthetic data in a Shiny app

Source: R/app.R
run_synthcheck_app.Rd

Experimental. run_synthcheck_app() opens an app that walks through the whole workflow in five tabs:

Usage

run_synthcheck_app(
  real = NULL,
  synthetic = NULL,
  host = "127.0.0.1",
  port = NULL,
  launch.browser = TRUE
)

Arguments

real

optional data frame of real responses, loaded into the Compare tab.

synthetic

optional data frame of synthetic respondents (for example from generate_synthetic() or read_synthetic()), loaded into the Compare tab.

host, port

where to serve the app. The default serves it on your own computer only.

launch.browser

open the app in a browser?

Value

Invisibly, when the app is closed with its Close button: A list with synthetic (the generated data), benchmark (the authenticity_benchmark() result, if one was run), instrument and personas.

Details

  1. Instrument: Upload an item table or use the IPIP-HEXACO items, and set the response scale and instructions (sc_instrument()).

  2. Personas: Type, upload or build the personas that take the instrument (sc_personas(), sc_persona_grid()).

Both upload panels offer a template to fill in. The templates are also in the package: system.file("templates", "instrument_template.csv", package = "synthcheck") and "personas_template.csv".

  1. Models: Add Anthropic, OpenAI or local Ollama models with their temperature, enter API keys, choose the number of attempts and respondents, and run generate_synthetic() with a progress bar and the time left.

  2. Compare: Load real data and run authenticity_benchmark(), with gg_benchmark(), gg_behaviour() and a plain-language summary per model (summarise_benchmark()).

  3. Export: Download the data (CSV, JSON, RDS or Excel), the benchmark and an R script that repeats the comparison.

API keys typed into the app stay in memory for that session only: They are never written to the saved data, the run settings or the R script. Keys set as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY (for example in .Renviron) are used without being shown. The app runs on your own computer; do not deploy it on a shared server with keys typed in.

Runs go to a background R process when callr is installed, so the app stays responsive and the Stop button works. Every attempt is written to the output folder as soon as it is done.

Synthetic respondents are experimental: The benchmark compares models and supports decisions about them. It does not show that synthetic data can replace a field test.

See also

generate_synthetic(), authenticity_benchmark()

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  res <- run_synthcheck_app()
  res$benchmark
}
